2.13.s:
2.61
puṣkara uvāca ..
rājadharmavrataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kṛtvā puruṣavigraham ..
pūruṣānviniyuñjīta cottamādhamakarmasu .. 1..
2.13.d:
2.61
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
राजधर्मव्रतं श्रेष्ठं कृत्वा पुरुषविग्रहम् ॥
पूरुषान्विनियुञ्जीत चोत्तमाधमकर्मसु ॥ 1॥
2.13.m: 2.61 / Puṣkara said: / Having taken the supreme observance of the duties of kings as [his] personal form, / he should appoint men to high and low tasks.

2.13.s:
grāmasyādhipatiṃ kuryāddaśagrāmādhipaṃ tathā ..
śatagrāmādhipaṃ cāpi tathaiva viṣayeśvaram .. 2 ..
2.13.d:
ग्रामस्याधिपतिं कुर्याद्दशग्रामाधिपं तथा ॥
शतग्रामाधिपं चापि तथैव विषयेश्वरम् ॥ 2 ॥
2.13.m: He should appoint a lord of a village, a lord of ten villages, / a lord of a hundred villages, and likewise a lord of a district.

2.13.s:
teṣāṃ bhāgavibhāgaśca bhavetkarmānurūpataḥ ..
nityameva tathā kāryaṃ teṣāṃ cāraiḥ parīkṣayet .. 3 ..
2.13.d:
तेषां भागविभागश्च भवेत्कर्मानुरूपतः ॥
नित्यमेव तथा कार्यं तेषां चारैः परीक्षयेत् ॥ 3 ॥
2.13.m: And their division of shares should be in accordance with their tasks; / he should always examine their duty by means of spies.

2.13.s:
grāmadoṣānsamutpannāngrāmeśaḥ praśamaṃ nayen ..
aśaktau deśapālasya sa tu gatvā nivedayet .. 4 ..
2.13.d:
ग्रामदोषान्समुत्पन्नान्ग्रामेशः प्रशमं नयेन् ॥
अशक्तौ देशपालस्य स तु गत्वा निवेदयेत् ॥ 4 ॥
2.13.m: The village lord should pacify faults that have arisen in the village; / if unable, he should go and report to the protector of the region.

2.13.s:
śrutvā tu deśapālopi tatra yuktimupācaret ..
sopyaśaktaḥ śateśāya yathāvadvinivedayet .. 5 ..
2.13.d:
श्रुत्वा तु देशपालोपि तत्र युक्तिमुपाचरेत् ॥
सोप्यशक्तः शतेशाय यथावद्विनिवेदयेत् ॥ 5 ॥
2.13.m: Having heard, the protector of the region too should employ a remedy there; / he, if unable, should properly report to the lord of a hundred [villages].

2.13.s:
śateśo viṣayeśāya sopi rājñe nivedayet ..
aśaktau śaktimān rāma svayaṃ yuktimupācaret .. 6 ..
2.13.d:
शतेशो विषयेशाय सोपि राज्ञे निवेदयेत् ॥
अशक्तौ शक्तिमान् राम स्वयं युक्तिमुपाचरेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.13.m: The lord of a hundred [villages should report] to the lord of the district, and he should report to the king; / if [they are] unable, one who is capable should personally employ a remedy, O Rāma.

2.13.s:
rājā sarvātmanā kuryādviṣaye rāma rakṣaṇam ..
vittamāpnoti dharmajña viṣayācca surakṣitāt .. 7 ..
2.13.d:
राजा सर्वात्मना कुर्याद्विषये राम रक्षणम् ॥
वित्तमाप्नोति धर्मज्ञ विषयाच्च सुरक्षितात् ॥ 7 ॥
2.13.m: The king should protect the district with all his heart, O Rāma; / one who knows dharma obtains wealth from a well-protected district.

2.13.s:
ripughātasamarthaḥ syādvittavāneva pārthivaḥ ..
paracakropamardeṣu vittavāneva mucyate .. 8 ..
2.13.d:
रिपुघातसमर्थः स्याद्वित्तवानेव पार्थिवः ॥
परचक्रोपमर्देषु वित्तवानेव मुच्यते ॥ 8 ॥
2.13.m: Only a king possessing wealth can be capable of striking down foes; / in the crushing [attacks] of an enemy's army, only one possessing wealth is delivered.

2.13.s:
vittavāneva sahati sudīrghamapi vigraham ..
bahudaṇḍānapi parāṃstathā bhindyāddhanādhipaḥ .. 9 ..
2.13.d:
वित्तवानेव सहति सुदीर्घमपि विग्रहम् ॥
बहुदण्डानपि परांस्तथा भिन्द्याद्धनाधिपः ॥ 9 ॥
2.13.m: Only one possessing wealth endures even a very long war; / so too, a lord of wealth can break even enemies with large forces.

2.13.s:
anne prāṇāḥ prajāḥ sarvā dhane tacca pratiṣṭhitam ..
dhanavāndharmamāpnoti dhanavānkāmamaśnute .. 2.61.10 ..
2.13.d:
अन्ने प्राणाः प्रजाः सर्वा धने तच्च प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
धनवान्धर्ममाप्नोति धनवान्काममश्नुते ॥ 2.61.10 ॥
2.13.m: In food are the life-breaths of all subjects, and that is grounded in wealth; / one who possesses wealth attains dharma; one who possesses wealth enjoys pleasure.

2.13.s:
yasyārthastasya mitrāṇi yasyārthastasya bandhavāḥ ..
yasyārthaḥ sa pumām̐lloke yasyārthaḥ sopi paṇḍitaḥ .. 11 ..
2.13.d:
यस्यार्थस्तस्य मित्राणि यस्यार्थस्तस्य बन्धवाः ॥
यस्यार्थः स पुमाम्̐ल्लोके यस्यार्थः सोपि पण्डितः ॥ 11 ॥
2.13.m: He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen; / he who has wealth is a real man in the world; he who has wealth is also learned.

2.13.s:
arthena hi vihīnasya puruṣasyālpamedhasaḥ ..
vicchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā ..12..
2.13.d:
अर्थेन हि विहीनस्य पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसः ॥
विच्छिद्यन्ते क्रियाः सर्वा ग्रीष्मे कुसरितो यथा ॥12॥
2.13.m: For of a man of little intelligence who is devoid of wealth, / all undertakings are cut short, like poor streams in summer.

2.13.s:
viśeṣo nāsti lokeṣu patitasyādhanasya ca ..
patitānāṃ na gṛhṇanti daridro na prayacchati ..13 ..
2.13.d:
विशेषो नास्ति लोकेषु पतितस्याधनस्य च ॥
पतितानां न गृह्णन्ति दरिद्रो न प्रयच्छति ॥13 ॥
2.13.m: In this world, there is no difference between a fallen outcaste and a wealthless man: / they do not accept [gifts] from outcastes, and a poor man does not give.

2.13.s:
dhanahīnasya bhāryāpi naiva syādvaśavartinī ..
guṇaughamapi caivāsya naiva kaścitprakāśayet .. 14 ..
2.13.d:
धनहीनस्य भार्यापि नैव स्याद्वशवर्तिनी ॥
गुणौघमपि चैवास्य नैव कश्चित्प्रकाशयेत् ॥ 14 ॥
2.13.m: Even the wife of one who is destitute of wealth does not remain obedient; / and no one will bring to light his multitude of virtues.

2.13.s:
bāndhavā vinivartante dhanahīnāttathā narāt ..
yathā puṣpaphalairhīnācchakuntā dvija pādapāt .. .. 15 ..
2.13.d:
बान्धवा विनिवर्तन्ते धनहीनात्तथा नरात् ॥
यथा पुष्पफलैर्हीनाच्छकुन्ता द्विज पादपात् ॥ ॥ 15 ॥
2.13.m: Kinsmen turn away from a wealthless man, O twice-born, / just as birds [turn away] from a tree devoid of flowers and fruit.

2.13.s:
dāridryamaraṇe cobhe keṣāṃcitsadṛśe mate ..
satyaṃ hāsāddaridrasya mṛtaḥ śreyānmate mama .. 16 ..
2.13.d:
दारिद्र्यमरणे चोभे केषांचित्सदृशे मते ॥
सत्यं हासाद्दरिद्रस्य मृतः श्रेयान्मते मम ॥ 16 ॥
2.13.m: Both poverty and death are considered equal by some; / in truth, because of the mockery of a poor man, in my opinion a dead man is better.

2.13.s:
kośaṃ rājyatarormūlaṃ tasmādyatnaṃ tadarjane ..
dharmeṇaiva tataḥ kuryānnādharmeṇa kathaṃcana .. 17 ..
2.13.d:
कोशं राज्यतरोर्मूलं तस्माद्यत्नं तदर्जने ॥
धर्मेणैव ततः कुर्यान्नाधर्मेण कथंचन ॥ 17 ॥
2.13.m: The treasury is the root of the tree of the kingdom; therefore, one should strive to acquire it; / one should do so only through dharma, never through adharma.

2.13.s:
dhanairadharmasamprāptairyaddṛḍhaṃ hi pidhīyate ..
tadeva yāti vistāraṃ vināśāya durātmanām ..18 ..
2.13.d:
धनैरधर्मसम्प्राप्तैर्यद्दृढं हि पिधीयते ॥
तदेव याति विस्तारं विनाशाय दुरात्मनाम् ॥18 ॥
2.13.m: Whatever is firmly concealed by means of wealth obtained through adharma / expands precisely for the destruction of the wicked.

2.13.s:
sukṛtasya purāṇasya balena balināṃ vara ..
yadyadharmātphalaṃ śīghraṃ nāpnuvanti durātmanaḥ .. 19 ..
2.13.d:
सुकृतस्य पुराणस्य बलेन बलिनां वर ॥
यद्यधर्मात्फलं शीघ्रं नाप्नुवन्ति दुरात्मनः ॥ 19 ॥
2.13.m: If, by the strength of former good deeds, O best among the strong, / wicked men do not swiftly obtain the fruit of adharma,

2.13.s:
tathāpi pūrvakarmānte tena pāpena karmaṇā ..
vinaśyanti samūlāste saputradhanabāndhavāḥ .. 2.61.20 ..
2.13.d:
तथापि पूर्वकर्मान्ते तेन पापेन कर्मणा ॥
विनश्यन्ति समूलास्ते सपुत्रधनबान्धवाः ॥ 2.61.20 ॥
2.13.m: even so, at the end of their previous karma, through that evil action / they perish together with their roots, along with their sons, wealth, and kinsmen.

2.13.s:
narakeṣu tathā teṣāṃ yātanā vividhāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
bahūnyabdasahasrāṇi ye nṛpā rāṣṭrapīḍakāḥ .. 21 ..
2.13.d:
नरकेषु तथा तेषां यातना विविधाः स्मृताः ॥
बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि ये नृपा राष्ट्रपीडकाः ॥ 21 ॥
2.13.m: So too, various torments in hells are recorded for them / for many thousands of years—those kings who oppress their realm.

2.13.s:
nityaṃ rājñā tathā bhāvyaṃ garbhiṇīsahadharmiṇā ..
yathā svaṃ sukhamutsṛjya garbhasya sukhamāvahet . 22 ..
2.13.d:
नित्यं राज्ञा तथा भाव्यं गर्भिणीसहधर्मिणा ॥
यथा स्वं सुखमुत्सृज्य गर्भस्य सुखमावहेत् । 22 ॥
2.13.m: The king should constantly behave like a pregnant woman: / just as she, giving up her own comfort, secures the comfort of her womb,

2.13.s:
garbhiṇī tadvadeveha bhāvyaṃ bhūpatinā sadā ..
prajāsukhaṃ tu kartavyaṃ sukhamuddiśya cātmanaḥ .. 23 ..
2.13.d:
गर्भिणी तद्वदेवेह भाव्यं भूपतिना सदा ॥
प्रजासुखं तु कर्तव्यं सुखमुद्दिश्य चात्मनः ॥ 23 ॥
2.13.m: just so must a ruler of the earth always be here; / he must bring about the happiness of his subjects, keeping his own happiness in view.

2.13.s:
kiṃ yajñaistapasā tasya prajā yasya surakṣitāḥ ..
surakṣitāḥ prajāstasya svargastasya gṛhopamaḥ .. .. 24 ..
2.13.d:
किं यज्ञैस्तपसा तस्य प्रजा यस्य सुरक्षिताः ॥
सुरक्षिताः प्रजास्तस्य स्वर्गस्तस्य गृहोपमः ॥ ॥ 24 ॥
2.13.m: What need of sacrifices or asceticism has he whose subjects are well protected? / He whose subjects are well protected has heaven like his home.

2.13.s:
arakṣitāḥ prajā yasya narakaṃ tasya mandiram ..
rājā ṣaḍbhāgamādatte sukṛtādduṣkṛtādapi .. 25 ..
2.13.d:
अरक्षिताः प्रजा यस्य नरकं तस्य मन्दिरम् ॥
राजा षड्भागमादत्ते सुकृताद्दुष्कृतादपि ॥ 25 ॥
2.13.m: He whose subjects are unprotected has hell as his abode; / a king takes a sixth share from good deeds and from bad deeds.

2.13.s:
dharmo nāma mahābhāga sampadrakṣaṇa tatparaḥ ..
arakṣitastathā sarvaṃ pāpamāpnoti bhārgava .. 26 ..
2.13.d:
धर्मो नाम महाभाग सम्पद्रक्षण तत्परः ॥
अरक्षितस्तथा सर्वं पापमाप्नोति भार्गव ॥ 26 ॥
2.13.m: Dharma, O fortunate one, is intent on the protection of prosperity; / when it is unprotected, O Bhārgava, he incurs all the sin.

2.13.s:
naiva kiñcidavāpnoti puṇyabhākpṛthivīpatiḥ ..
āpannamapi dharmiṣṭhaṃ prajā rakṣatyathāpadi. . 27 ..
2.13.d:
नैव किञ्चिदवाप्नोति पुण्यभाक्पृथिवीपतिः ॥
आपन्नमपि धर्मिष्ठं प्रजा रक्षत्यथापदि॥ 27 ॥
2.13.m: A lord of the earth who takes a share of merit receives nothing at all [of it]; / the righteous [king] who has fallen into misfortune, however, protects his subjects in misfortune.

2.13.s:
tasmāddharmārthakāmena prajā rakṣyā mahīkṣitā ..
subhagaiścātha durvṛttarājavallabhataskaraiḥ .. 28 ..
2.13.d:
तस्माद्धर्मार्थकामेन प्रजा रक्ष्या महीक्षिता ॥
सुभगैश्चाथ दुर्वृत्तराजवल्लभतस्करैः ॥ 28 ॥
2.13.m: Therefore, desiring dharma and wealth, subjects must be protected by a ruler of the earth / from favorites, and from wicked royal favorites and thieves.

2.13.s:
bhakṣyamāṇāḥ prajā rakṣyā kāyasthaiśca viśeṣataḥ ..
rakṣitāstadbhayebhyastu prajā rājñāṃ bhavanti tāḥ .. 29 ..
2.13.d:
भक्ष्यमाणाः प्रजा रक्ष्या कायस्थैश्च विशेषतः ॥
रक्षितास्तद्भयेभ्यस्तु प्रजा राज्ञां भवन्ति ताः ॥ 29 ॥
2.13.m: Subjects being devoured must be protected, especially from scribes; / protected from those fears, they become the subjects of kings.

2.13.s:
arakṣitā sā bhavati teṣāmeveha bhojanam ..
sādhusaṃrakṣaṇārthāya rājā duṣṭa nibarhaṇam .. 2.61.30 ..
2.13.d:
अरक्षिता सा भवति तेषामेवेह भोजनम् ॥
साधुसंरक्षणार्थाय राजा दुष्ट निबर्हणम् ॥ 2.61.30 ॥
2.13.m: Unprotected, they become the very food of those [oppressors] here; / for the sake of protecting the virtuous, the king should always bring about the destruction of the wicked,

2.13.s:
tṛṇānāmiva nirmātā sadā kuryājjitendriyaḥ ..
śāstroktaṃ balimādadyāddharmaṃ tattasya jīvitam .. 31 ..
2.13.d:
तृणानामिव निर्माता सदा कुर्याज्जितेन्द्रियः ॥
शास्त्रोक्तं बलिमादद्याद्धर्मं तत्तस्य जीवितम् ॥ 31 ॥
2.13.m: like a weeder of grasses, having his senses subdued; / he should take the tribute prescribed by the treatises: that dharma is his livelihood.

2.13.s:
tasya santyajanaṃ rājā na samṛddhopi kārayet ..
ākārāṇi ca sarvāṇi śulkaṃ śāstrodito baliḥ .. 32 ..
2.13.d:
तस्य सन्त्यजनं राजा न समृद्धोपि कारयेत् ॥
आकाराणि च सर्वाणि शुल्कं शास्त्रोदितो बलिः ॥ 32 ॥
2.13.m: The king, even if prosperous, should not abandon that; / and all mines, custom duties, and the tribute prescribed by the treatises,

2.13.s:
daṇḍaṃ vinayanādrājño dharmyaṃ tattasya jīvitam ..
dhartā karāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ prabhurukto mahīpatiḥ .. 33 ..
2.13.d:
दण्डं विनयनाद्राज्ञो धर्म्यं तत्तस्य जीवितम् ॥
धर्ता कराणां सर्वेषां प्रभुरुक्तो महीपतिः ॥ 33 ॥
2.13.m: and the fine derived from the king's administration of justice—that is his lawful livelihood; / the lord of the earth is declared to be the master and bearer of all taxes.

2.13.s:
nidhiṃ purāṇaṃ saṃprāpya keśavaṃ tu praveśayet ..
arthaṃ brāhmaṇasātkuryāddharmakāmo mahīpatiḥ .. .. 34 ..
2.13.d:
निधिं पुराणं संप्राप्य केशवं तु प्रवेशयेत् ॥
अर्थं ब्राह्मणसात्कुर्याद्धर्मकामो महीपतिः ॥ ॥ 34 ॥
2.13.m: Having found an ancient treasure, he should offer it to Keśava; / the lord of the earth who desires dharma should hand over the wealth to the brahmins.

2.13.s:
nidhiṃ dvijottamaḥ prāpya gṛhṇīyātsakalaṃ tathā ..
jagatosya samagrasya prabhurukto dvijottamaḥ .. 35..
2.13.d:
निधिं द्विजोत्तमः प्राप्य गृह्णीयात्सकलं तथा ॥
जगतोस्य समग्रस्य प्रभुरुक्तो द्विजोत्तमः ॥ 35॥
2.13.m: An eminent twice-born, having found a treasure, may take it entirely; / for an eminent twice-born is declared to be the master of this entire world.

2.13.s:
nidhiṃ jñātvā purāṇaṃ tu kṣatraviṭśūdrayonayaḥ ..
nivedayeyurbhūpāya rājā labdhvāpi taṃ nidhim .. 36 ..
2.13.d:
निधिं ज्ञात्वा पुराणं तु क्षत्रविट्शूद्रयोनयः ॥
निवेदयेयुर्भूपाय राजा लब्ध्वापि तं निधिम् ॥ 36 ॥
2.13.m: Those born of kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra wombs, having discovered an ancient treasure, / should report it to the king; and the king, having obtained that treasure,

2.13.s:
caturthamaṣṭamaṃ cāṃśaṃ tathā ṣoḍaśamaṃ dvija ..
varṇakrameṇa visṛjedākhyātaṃ dharma kāraṇam .. 37 ..
2.13.d:
चतुर्थमष्टमं चांशं तथा षोडशमं द्विज ॥
वर्णक्रमेण विसृजेदाख्यातं धर्म कारणम् ॥ 37 ॥
2.13.m: should release a fourth, an eighth, and a sixteenth share, O twice-born, / in order of the social classes: this is declared as the basis of dharma.

2.13.s:
te'pi labdhvā tadā tena saṃvibhajya dvijottamān ..
śeṣeṇa kuryuḥ kāmārthau viditau pṛthivīpateḥ .. 38 ..
2.13.d:
तेऽपि लब्ध्वा तदा तेन संविभज्य द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
शेषेण कुर्युः कामार्थौ विदितौ पृथिवीपतेः ॥ 38 ॥
2.13.m: They too, having obtained it then from him, having shared it with eminent twice-born, / should pursue pleasure and wealth with the remainder, with the knowledge of the ruler of the earth.

2.13.s:
prakāśavibhavo loke yasya rājñaḥ sa bhūpatiḥ ..
aprakāśadhano yastu narakaṃ tasya mandiram .. 39 ..
2.13.d:
प्रकाशविभवो लोके यस्य राज्ञः स भूपतिः ॥
अप्रकाशधनो यस्तु नरकं तस्य मन्दिरम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.13.m: He alone is a king in this world whose wealth is made manifest; / but for him whose wealth is unmanifest [or illicit], hell is his dwelling.

2.13.s:
mamedamiti yo brūyānnidhiṃ satyena mānavaḥ ..
tasyādadīta nṛpatirbhāgamabrāhmaṇasya tu .. 2.61.40 ..
2.13.d:
ममेदमिति यो ब्रूयान्निधिं सत्येन मानवः ॥
तस्याददीत नृपतिर्भागमब्राह्मणस्य तु ॥ 2.61.40 ॥
2.13.m: If a man should truthfully say of a treasure, "This is mine," / the king should take a share from him, provided he is not a brahmin.

2.13.s:
caturviṃśatikaṃ rāma dvādaśaṃ ṣaṣṭhameva ca ..
kṣatriyāśca tathā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāśca bhṛgunandana .. 41 ..
2.13.d:
चतुर्विंशतिकं राम द्वादशं षष्ठमेव च ॥
क्षत्रियाश्च तथा वैश्याः शूद्राश्च भृगुनन्दन ॥ 41 ॥
2.13.m: A twenty-fourth part, O Rāma, a twelfth part, and a sixth part / from kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, O son of Bhṛgu.

2.13.s:
anṛtaṃ ca vadandaṇḍyaḥ svavittasyāṃśamaṣṭakam ..
praṇaṣṭasvāmikaṃ rikthaṃ rājā tryabdaṃ nidhāpayet .. 42 ..
2.13.d:
अनृतं च वदन्दण्ड्यः स्ववित्तस्यांशमष्टकम् ॥
प्रणष्टस्वामिकं रिक्थं राजा त्र्यब्दं निधापयेत् ॥ 42 ॥
2.13.m: And if he speaks an untruth, he should be fined an eighth part of his own wealth. / The king should cause ownerless property to be kept deposited for three years.

2.13.s:
arvāktryabdāddharetsvāmī pareṇa nṛpatirharet ..
mamedamiti yo brūyādanuyukto yathāvidhi .. 43 ..
2.13.d:
अर्वाक्त्र्यब्दाद्धरेत्स्वामी परेण नृपतिर्हरेत् ॥
ममेदमिति यो ब्रूयादनुयुक्तो यथाविधि ॥ 43 ॥
2.13.m: Within three years the owner may take it; after that, the king may take it. / If, upon being questioned according to rule, one should say, "This is mine,"

2.13.s:
saṃpādya rūpaṃ dravyādīnsvāmī taddravyamarhati ..
avedayāno naṣṭasya deśaṃ kālaṃ ca tattvataḥ .. .. 44 ..
2.13.d:
संपाद्य रूपं द्रव्यादीन्स्वामी तद्द्रव्यमर्हति ॥
अवेदयानो नष्टस्य देशं कालं च तत्त्वतः ॥ ॥ 44 ॥
2.13.m: the owner is entitled to that property after establishing its form, the substance, and so on. / If he fails to state accurately the place and time of its loss,

2.13.s:
varṇarūpaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca tatsamaṃ daṇḍamarhati ..
nidhivadbhāgamādadyātpranaṣṭādhigatānnṛpaḥ ..45..
2.13.d:
वर्णरूपं प्रमाणं च तत्समं दण्डमर्हति ॥
निधिवद्भागमादद्यात्प्रनष्टाधिगतान्नृपः ॥45॥
2.13.m: its colour, form, and quantity, he deserves a fine equal to it. / The king should take a share from lost property that has been recovered, just as from a treasure.

2.13.s:
bāladāyādikaṃ rikthaṃ tāvadrājā tu pālayet ..
yāvatsa syātsamāvṛtto yāvadvātītaśaiśavaḥ .. 46 ..
2.13.d:
बालदायादिकं रिक्थं तावद्राजा तु पालयेत् ॥
यावत्स स्यात्समावृत्तो यावद्वातीतशैशवः ॥ 46 ॥
2.13.m: The king should protect the inheritance of a minor heir / until he has returned from his studies, or until his childhood has passed.

2.13.s:
bālaputreṣu caivaṃ syādrakṣaṇaṃ niṣkulāsu ca ..
pativratāsu ca strīṣu vidhavāsvāturāsu ca .. .. 47 ..
2.13.d:
बालपुत्रेषु चैवं स्याद्रक्षणं निष्कुलासु च ॥
पतिव्रतासु च स्त्रीषु विधवास्वातुरासु च ॥ ॥ 47 ॥
2.13.m: There should be similar protection for women with infant sons, for those without kin, / for faithful wives, and for widows who are afflicted with illness.

2.13.s:
jīvantīnāṃ tu tāsāṃ ye dhārayeyuḥ svabāndhavāḥ ..
tāñchiṣyāccauradaṇḍena dhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ .. 48 ..
2.13.d:
जीवन्तीनां तु तासां ये धारयेयुः स्वबान्धवाः ॥
ताञ्छिष्याच्चौरदण्डेन धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः ॥ 48 ॥
2.13.m: If their own kinsmen should seize [their wealth] while they are still living, / a righteous king should punish them with the punishment for a thief.

2.13.s:
sarveṣāmeva varṇānāṃ caurairapahṛtaṃ dhanam ..
tatpramāṇaṃ svakātkośāddātavyamavidhārayan .. 49 ..
2.13.d:
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां चौरैरपहृतं धनम् ॥
तत्प्रमाणं स्वकात्कोशाद्दातव्यमविधारयन् ॥ 49 ॥
2.13.m: If wealth belonging to [members of] any of the classes has been stolen by thieves, / he must, without hesitating, give [them] that amount from his own treasury.

2.13.s:
tatastu paścātkartavyaṃ caurānveṣaṇamañjasā ..
caurarakṣādhikāribhyo rājāpi tadavāpnuyāt .. 2.61.50 ..
2.13.d:
ततस्तु पश्चात्कर्तव्यं चौरान्वेषणमञ्जसा ॥
चौररक्षाधिकारिभ्यो राजापि तदवाप्नुयात् ॥ 2.61.50 ॥
2.13.m: Then, afterwards, a search for the thieves should be made swiftly. / The king too may recover that [amount] from the officers in charge of guarding against thieves.

2.13.s:
ahṛte ca tathā vitte hṛtamityeva vādinam ..
nirdhanaṃ pārthivaḥ kṛtvā viṣayātsvādvivāsayet .. 51 ..
2.13.d:
अहृते च तथा वित्ते हृतमित्येव वादिनम् ॥
निर्धनं पार्थिवः कृत्वा विषयात्स्वाद्विवासयेत् ॥ 51 ॥
2.13.m: And if wealth has not been taken, but one claims, "It has been taken," / the king should make him destitute and banish him from his realm.

2.13.s:
na tadrājñā pradātavyaṃ gṛhe yatparicārakaiḥ ..
pracaradbhirhṛtaṃ dravyaṃ kāryaṃ tatrānvavekṣaṇam .. 52 ..
2.13.d:
न तद्राज्ञा प्रदातव्यं गृहे यत्परिचारकैः ॥
प्रचरद्भिर्हृतं द्रव्यं कार्यं तत्रान्ववेक्षणम् ॥ 52 ॥
2.13.m: That property which has been stolen in the house by servants / moving about should not be paid out by the king; an investigation must be made into it.

2.13.s:
svarāṣṭrapaṇyādādadyādrājā viṃśatimaṃ dvija ..
śulkāṃśaṃ paradeśācca nibodha gadato mama .. 53 ..
2.13.d:
स्वराष्ट्रपण्यादादद्याद्राजा विंशतिमं द्विज ॥
शुल्कांशं परदेशाच्च निबोध गदतो मम ॥ 53 ॥
2.13.m: The king should take a twentieth part as a portion of customs duty / from merchandise of his own realm, O twice-born, and from a foreign land—listen as I speak:

2.13.s:
kṣayavyayapravāsāṃśca yathāyāmaṃ dvijottama! ..
jñātvā tu kalpayettatra śulkāṃśaṃ pṛthavīpatiḥ .. 54 ..
2.13.d:
क्षयव्ययप्रवासांश्च यथायामं द्विजोत्तम! ॥
ज्ञात्वा तु कल्पयेत्तत्र शुल्कांशं पृथवीपतिः ॥ 54 ॥
2.13.m: Having ascertained the depreciation, expenses, and travel, as well as the distance, O foremost of the twice-born, / the king should determine the portion of customs duty in that matter.

2.13.s:
tathā kāryaṃ yathā lābhaṃ vaṇijaḥ samavāpnuyuḥ ..
puṇyacchedaśca naiva syātsvadeśe pṛthavīpateḥ .. 55 ..
2.13.d:
तथा कार्यं यथा लाभं वणिजः समवाप्नुयुः ॥
पुण्यच्छेदश्च नैव स्यात्स्वदेशे पृथवीपतेः ॥ 55 ॥
2.13.m: It should be done in such a way that the merchants obtain a profit, / and there is no loss of merit in the realm of the king.

2.13.s:
vyayaṃ śulkapravāsādi laṅghayitvā tathā dvija ..
viṃśāṃśabhāgamādadyurdaṇḍanīyā atonyathā .. 56 ..
2.13.d:
व्ययं शुल्कप्रवासादि लङ्घयित्वा तथा द्विज ॥
विंशांशभागमादद्युर्दण्डनीया अतोन्यथा ॥ 56 ॥
2.13.m: Having thus deducted the expenses, toll, travel, and the like, O twice-born, / they should take a twentieth share; otherwise they are to be punished.

2.13.s:
diśi diśyekameva syācchulkasthānaṃ nṛpasya tu ..
tadatikramato dravyaṃ rājagāmi vidhīyate .. 57 ..
2.13.d:
दिशि दिश्येकमेव स्याच्छुल्कस्थानं नृपस्य तु ॥
तदतिक्रमतो द्रव्यं राजगामि विधीयते ॥ 57 ॥
2.13.m: In each direction there should be only a single toll station belonging to the king; / through bypassing that, the property is ordained to go to the king.

2.13.s:
dūtānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca rājājñāgāmināṃ tathā ..
strīṇāṃ pravrajitānāṃ ca tāraśulkaṃ vivarjayet .. 58 ..
2.13.d:
दूतानां ब्राह्मणानां च राजाज्ञागामिनां तथा ॥
स्त्रीणां प्रव्रजितानां च तारशुल्कं विवर्जयेत् ॥ 58 ॥
2.13.m: One should exempt envoys, brahmins, / those travelling on the king's business, women, and renunciants from the ferry toll.

2.13.s:
bhinnakarṣāpaṇaṃ śulkaṃ na grāhyaṃ pṛthivīkṣitā ..
tāreṣu dāśadoṣeṇa naṣṭaṃ dāśātpradāpayet .. 59 ..
2.13.d:
भिन्नकर्षापणं शुल्कं न ग्राह्यं पृथिवीक्षिता ॥
तारेषु दाशदोषेण नष्टं दाशात्प्रदापयेत् ॥ 59 ॥
2.13.m: A toll that is a fraction of a kārṣāpaṇa should not be taken by the ruler of the earth. / If [goods are] lost at ferries through the boatman's fault, he should cause the boatman to make it good.

2.13.s:
daivadoṣavinaṣṭaṃ ca naṣṭaṃ yasyaiva tasya tat ..
śūkadhānyeṣu ṣaḍbhāgaṃ śiṃbidhānyeṣvathāṣṭakam .. 2.61.60 ..
2.13.d:
दैवदोषविनष्टं च नष्टं यस्यैव तस्य तत् ॥
शूकधान्येषु षड्भागं शिंबिधान्येष्वथाष्टकम् ॥ 2.61.60 ॥
2.13.m: And what is destroyed through an act of fate is lost only to him to whom it belonged. / A sixth share on bearded grains, and an eighth on legumes,

2.13.s:
rājā balyarthamādadyāddeśakālānurūpakam ..
rājāṃśabhāgamādadyādrājā paśuhiraṇyayoḥ .. 61 ..
2.13.d:
राजा बल्यर्थमादद्याद्देशकालानुरूपकम् ॥
राजांशभागमादद्याद्राजा पशुहिरण्ययोः ॥ 61 ॥
2.13.m: the king should take as tribute, in accordance with the place and time. / The king should take the king's share of cattle and gold,

2.13.s:
gandhauṣadhirasānāṃ ca puṣpamūlaphalasya ca ..
patraśākatṛṇānāṃ ca vatsareṇa ca carmaṇām .. 65 ..
2.13.d:
गन्धौषधिरसानां च पुष्पमूलफलस्य च ॥
पत्रशाकतृणानां च वत्सरेण च चर्मणाम् ॥ 65 ॥
2.13.m: of perfumes, medicinal herbs, and plant juices, of flowers, roots, and fruits, / of leaves, vegetables, and grass, and every year of hides,

2.13.s:
vaidalānāṃ ca bhāṃḍānāṃ sarvasyāśmamayasya ca ..
ṣaḍbhāgameva cādadyādbrāhmaṇebhyastathā karam .. 63 ..
2.13.d:
वैदलानां च भांडानां सर्वस्याश्ममयस्य च ॥
षड्भागमेव चादद्याद्ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तथा करम् ॥ 63 ॥
2.13.m: of split-reed vessels, and of everything made of stone. / And he should take only a sixth share as tax from brahmins.

2.13.s:
tebhyastaddharmalābhena rājño lābhaḥ paraṃ bhavet ..
na ca kṣudhāvasīdeta śrotriyo viṣaye vasan .. 64 ..
2.13.d:
तेभ्यस्तद्धर्मलाभेन राज्ञो लाभः परं भवेत् ॥
न च क्षुधावसीदेत श्रोत्रियो विषये वसन् ॥ 64 ॥
2.13.m: Through the gain of their dharma, the king receives the supreme gain. / A Vedic scholar dwelling in his realm must not waste away from hunger.

2.13.s:
yasya rājñastu viṣaye śrotriyaḥ sīdati kṣudhā ..
tasya sīdati tadrāṣṭraṃ durbhikṣavyādhitaskaraiḥ .. 65 ..
2.13.d:
यस्य राज्ञस्तु विषये श्रोत्रियः सीदति क्षुधा ॥
तस्य सीदति तद्राष्ट्रं दुर्भिक्षव्याधितस्करैः ॥ 65 ॥
2.13.m: The realm of that king in whose domain a Vedic scholar wastes away from hunger / wastes away through famine, disease, and thieves.

2.13.s:
śrutavṛtte tu vijñāya vṛttiṃ tasya prakalpayet ..
rakṣecca sarvatastvenaṃ pitā putramivaurasam .. 66 ..
2.13.d:
श्रुतवृत्ते तु विज्ञाय वृत्तिं तस्य प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
रक्षेच्च सर्वतस्त्वेनं पिता पुत्रमिवौरसम् ॥ 66 ॥
2.13.m: Having ascertained his learning and conduct, he should provide him a livelihood, / and he should protect him on every side, as a father protects his own son.

2.13.s:
saṃrakṣyamāṇo rājñā yaḥ kurute dharma saṃgraham ..
tenāyurvarddhate rājño draviṇaṃ rāṣṭrameva ca .. 67 ..
2.13.d:
संरक्ष्यमाणो राज्ञा यः कुरुते धर्म संग्रहम् ॥
तेनायुर्वर्द्धते राज्ञो द्रविणं राष्ट्रमेव च ॥ 67 ॥
2.13.m: By means of the accumulation of dharma that he performs when protected by the king, / the king's life, wealth, and realm increase.

2.13.s:
karma kuryurnarendrasya māsenaikaṃ ca śilpinaḥ ..
bhaktamātreṇa ye cānye svaśarīropajīvinaḥ .. 68 ..
2.13.d:
कर्म कुर्युर्नरेन्द्रस्य मासेनैकं च शिल्पिनः ॥
भक्तमात्रेण ये चान्ये स्वशरीरोपजीविनः ॥ 68 ॥
2.13.m: Artisans should do one [day of] work for the king in a month, / as well as other [labourers] who subsist on their own bodies, for mere food.

2.13.s:
snātānuliptāśca vibhūṣitāśca veśyāṅganāvāravivartitena ..
saṃvītagātraḥ pṛthivīśvarasya sadābhyupāsāṃ paritastrikuryuḥ .. ..69..
2.62
puṣkara uvāca ..
dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca puruṣārthaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
anyonyarakṣaṇātteṣāṃ sevā kāryā mahīkṣitā .. 1 ..
dharmamūlorthaviṭapastathā kāmaphalo mahān ..
trivargapādapastasya rakṣaṇātphalabhāgbhavet .. 2 ..
dharmāvirodhinī kāryā kāmasevā sadaiva tu ..
mūlacchede bhavennāśo viṭapasya phalasya ca ..3 ..
kāmasevāvihīnasya dharmārthāvapi niṣphalau ..
oṣadhīnāṃ phalārthāya kīnāśo yatnavāṃstathā ..4..
kāmārthī yatnavānevaṃ lobho dharmārthayordvija ..
kāmasyāpi paraṃ nāryo dharmarāgamadotkaṭāḥ .. 5 ..
tadarthaṃ ratnanidhayo vibhavāśca tathā pare ..
gītaṃ vādyaṃ sumadhuraṃ bhojyaṃ pānaṃ srajistathā ..6..
2.13.d:
स्नातानुलिप्ताश्च विभूषिताश्च वेश्याङ्गनावारविवर्तितेन ॥
संवीतगात्रः पृथिवीश्वरस्य सदाभ्युपासां परितस्त्रिकुर्युः ॥ ॥69॥
2.62
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च पुरुषार्थः परः स्मृतः ॥
अन्योन्यरक्षणात्तेषां सेवा कार्या महीक्षिता ॥ 1 ॥
धर्ममूलोर्थविटपस्तथा कामफलो महान् ॥
त्रिवर्गपादपस्तस्य रक्षणात्फलभाग्भवेत् ॥ 2 ॥
धर्माविरोधिनी कार्या कामसेवा सदैव तु ॥
मूलच्छेदे भवेन्नाशो विटपस्य फलस्य च ॥3 ॥
कामसेवाविहीनस्य धर्मार्थावपि निष्फलौ ॥
ओषधीनां फलार्थाय कीनाशो यत्नवांस्तथा ॥4॥
कामार्थी यत्नवानेवं लोभो धर्मार्थयोर्द्विज ॥
कामस्यापि परं नार्यो धर्मरागमदोत्कटाः ॥ 5 ॥
तदर्थं रत्ननिधयो विभवाश्च तथा परे ॥

Puṣkara said:
Dharma, wealth, and pleasure are regarded as the supreme ends of man. / They should be pursued by the ruler of the earth through protecting them mutually.
Dharma is the root, wealth the branch, and pleasure the great fruit; / through protecting that tree of the threefold group, he becomes a partaker of the fruit.
The pursuit of pleasure, however, should always be conducted without conflict with dharma; / if the root is cut, destruction of the branch and of the fruit ensues.
For one who is devoid of the pursuit of pleasure, even dharma and wealth are fruitless. / Just as a farmer makes effort for the sake of the fruit of plants,
so one seeking pleasure makes effort; passion is the [incentive] for dharma and wealth, O twice-born. / Women, moreover, intoxicated with passion and delight in dharma, are the highest [form] of pleasure.
For their sake exist treasures of jewels and other riches, / song, sweet instrumental music, food, drink, and garlands,

Meat attains firmness, or softness through ginger water; / through the addition of alkali from the varuṇa tree, fish bones dissolve.
Milk attains readiness with pieces of palāśa wood; / through the addition of wood-apple powder and fine [spices],
clarified butter becomes fragrant, as it does with burnt barley grains cast into it. / In lotus-water, through the addition of sour gruel, acidity develops.
Molasses and the like attain purification when combined with milk; / a color resembling ruby is produced by aṃśumatī
for drinks, O illustrious one, or whatever else one desires. / Through the addition of alkali, the sourness of a sour substance is removed.
Food that has definitely become unpalatable from an excess of salt cast into it / can attain good flavor through casting in balls of sand.
Through the addition of alkali from chickpeas, all flowers and fruits / quickly turn into liquid; and preparations may be made of those liquified substances.

His constant protection should be carried out through teachers with proper means; / and one should instruct him in dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, as well as the archery science.
And one should always make him exercise in chariot, horse, and elephant; / and one should likewise instruct him in the arts through trusted persons who falsely speak pleasantly.

2.13.m:
Having achieved the conquest of servants, the king should conquer the townspeople and countrymen; / and having achieved victory over them, he should then conquer external enemies.
And external enemies are to be known as threefold: equals, neighbours, and artificial ones. / They are heavier in the order given; toward them effort should always be directed.
Ancestral, a dependent, and likewise [the enemy] of an enemy, / and artificial, O fortunate one—an ally is said to be threefold.
Even so, the prior one is more significant, and among them also a dependent. / The sovereign, the minister, the countryside, the army, and likewise the fortress,
the treasury, and the ally, O knower of dharma, the kingdom is said to have seven limbs. / And of the seven-limbed kingdom, the sovereign is declared to be the root.
Since the limbs have their root in him, he must be protected with diligence; / and the protection of the six limbs must also be carried out by him with diligence.
Whoever of small mind commits treason against even one of the limbs, / his execution must be carried out immediately by the ruler of the earth.

2.13.m:
A king should not be gentle, for a gentle one is despised; / nor should he be harsh, for the people tremble before a fierce one.
He who is gentle at the right time and harsh at the right time, / a king looking to both worlds, gains both worlds.
The protector of the earth should avoid joking with servants; / servants here despise a king whose speech sparkles with merriment.
And the lord of the earth should avoid all vices; / for the sake of winning over the people, he may affect a feigned vice.
Towards a king of pride whose mind is constantly agitated, / the people become alienated because he is always difficult to serve.
The lord of the earth should speak to everyone with a smile first; / even among the common sort, O fortunate one, he should not knit his brows.
O best of upholders of dharma, the king must be generous; / the entire earth comes under the control of a generous man.

2.13.m:
And the king should be expeditious in all undertakings; / for a dilatory king, loss of work is certain.
In passion, arrogance, pride, treason, and sinful action, / and when unpleasant words must be spoken, a dilatory man is praised.
A king must be one whose counsel is concealed, O best of twice-born; / for one whose counsel is unconcealed, all misfortunes are known to be certain.
For that lord of the earth whose undertakings are known only when accomplished, / and not when begun, O fortunate one, the earth comes under his control.
A kingdom is always rooted in counsel; therefore, well-protected counsel / must always be maintained by rulers of the earth out of fear of betrayal of counsel.
Counsel mastered by one who knows counsel brings happiness to the self-restrained; / through the betrayal of counsel, many rulers of the earth have perished.
By appearance, by hints, by gait, by gesture, and by speech, / and by changes in eyes and face, the inner mind is known.

2.13.m:
The whole earth never comes under the control of that lord of the earth / who is not skilled in this, O son of Bhṛgu.
A king should not deliberate counsel alone, nor with many; / the king may deliberate counsels separately with many at will.
Even among ministers, a minister should not disclose counsel; / someone, somewhere is always trusted by men in this world.
And thus the determination of counsel should be made by a single wise man, / or the attainment of determination may come from living by another's intellect.
When an action has been firmly decided upon by the king alone, / he should further attend upon the brahmins and those sages versed in the three Vedas, O Rāma.
Not upon fools addicted to bad treatises, for they are thorns to the world; / and he should constantly serve aged brahmins who know the Vedas and are pure.
From them he should learn discipline, for one whose self is disciplined / can bring the entire earth under control, without doubt.

2.13.m:
Many kings, together with their retinues, have perished through lack of discipline; / and forest-dwellers have obtained kingdoms through discipline.
He should learn the three Vedas from those who know the threefold knowledge, and the eternal science of governance; / metaphysics, which is the knowledge of the self, [from the wise], and agriculture and commerce from ordinary people.
He should day and night practise yoga for conquering the senses; / for having conquered the senses, he is able to keep his subjects in submission.
The king should sacrifice with numerous rites accompanied by suitable sacrificial fees, / and for the sake of dharma he should give luxuries and wealth to brahmins.
Through trustworthy revenue collectors, he should gather tribute from the realm; / he should be devoted to the sacred tradition in the world, and behave like a father toward men.
Twice-born men who have returned from the teacher’s house should be honoured; / for this is prescribed as the inexhaustible brahminical treasure of kings.
Thieves do not seize it, nor do enemies take it away, nor is it lost; / therefore, an imperishable treasure should be deposited by the king among brahmins.

2.13.m:
When challenged by equals, superiors, or inferiors, the king, protecting his subjects, / should not turn back from battle, remembering the vow of a kṣatriya.
Not turning back in battles, protection of subjects, / and service to brahmins are the highest good for kings.
And for the wretched, the elderly, and widowed women, / he should likewise provide acquisition, preservation, and livelihood.
Moreover, the system of classes and stages of life must especially be maintained; / the king should redirect to their own duties those who have fallen from their own dharma.
To the hermitages he should personally convey, at the proper time, oil, vessels, and food, / honouring [the ascetics] and never slighting them.
He should diligently dedicate all his affairs, his kingdom, and his very self to the ascetic, / and he should worship him like a god.
Men must know two kinds of intellect: the straight and the crooked. / Having recognized deceitful persons, he should not associate with them once they have attained awareness.

2.13.m:
An enemy must not discover his vulnerability, but he should discover the vulnerability of the enemy; / he should conceal his limbs like a tortoise and guard his own weak point.
He should not trust the untrustworthy, nor excessively trust the trustworthy; / fear born of trust cuts down even the roots.
He should also make the enemy trust him by a plausible reason; / he should ponder interests like a heron, and exert valour like a lion.
He should snatch away like a heron, and dart away like a hare; / and the king should strike firmly like a boar.
He should have a diverse appearance like a peacock, be staunch in devotion like a blind man, / and the king should speak sweetly like a parrot or a cuckoo.
He should constantly be suspicious like a crow, and dwell in an unknown lodging; / and he should not touch food or a bed that has not been examined beforehand.
Likewise, O best of men, clothing, flowers, ornaments, or whatever else; / he should not plunge into a crowd of people, nor into an unknown body of water.
[Without] men who have been tested beforehand and act faithfully, / he should not mount an elephant, a vicious beast, or an unbroken horse.

2.13.m:
He should not visit an unknown woman, nor one wearing inauspicious garments; / he should not board an unsafe boat, nor one with an untested boatman.
And whoever might become adversaries while he conquers the earth, / all of them he should bring under control by means of conciliation and the other expedients.
In such a way that no emaciation comes upon the subjects through neglect, / the king, guarding his own realm, must govern.
If a king, through delusion, oppresses his own realm by neglect, / he soon falls from his kingdom and from life, together with his relatives.
Just as a calf, when nourished and full of strength, becomes fit for work, / even so, O fortunate one, a realm when nourished becomes great in productivity.
The king who fosters his realm and guards it well, / upon him the subjects depend for their livelihood, and he attains an immense reward.
Gold and grain should be yielded by the earth well protected by the king, / constantly from his own people and from others, just like a mother and a father.

2.67
Rāma said:
Expound the expedients beginning with conciliation, O highly splendid one, / and their characteristics as well as their application, O son of Varuṇa.
Puṣkara said:
Conciliation and division, O Rāma, as well as punishment, O best of men, / and negligence, trickery, and sorcery, O descendant of Bhṛgu—
seven applications have been spoken of. Listen to them as I speak. / Conciliation is said to be of two kinds: truthful and untruthful.
Even among those, what is untruthful turns into abuse against the virtuous; / and that which is pleasing to the virtuous—they are manageable by conciliation, not those [who are not virtuous], O Rāma.
Those born of noble lineage, upright, devoted to dharma, with conquered senses, / are manageable by conciliation; one should not employ untruthful conciliation toward them.
And truthful conciliation is to be made by describing family, character, and so forth; / likewise, both of these, O Rāma, and the praising of deeds done [for oneself],

and by that very method, proclaiming one’s own gratitude. / Thus, those intent on dharma are to be brought under control by soothing words.
Although there is the supreme traditional saying that "demons are captivated by conciliation," / even so, when applied to the wicked, it is unhelpful.
"A person speaking conciliatory words is deceitful"—thus / the wicked perceive him; therefore, it is avoided toward them.
Those who are of pure descent, upright, trusted, established in dharma, dedicated to truth, and modest, / and those who are always elevated in honor, O Rāma—those men are declared manageable by conciliation.
2.68
Puṣkara said:
Toward those who are corrupt toward one another, enraged, frightened, or humiliated, / one should employ division, for they are considered manageable by division.
Those who, out of a particular offense, fear the enemy, O Rāma, / are then to be intensely divided by protecting [them against] that offense.
One should show hope from one's own side, and show danger from the enemy's side. / In this way one should divide them, and bring the divided properly under control.

2.14.m:
For those united, without division, are hard to endure even for Śakra; / therefore, those skilled in policy praise division.
Whether the division [is heard] through one's own mouth or division through another's mouth, / having examined it well, I consider division heard through another's mouth to be good.
Those who are divided by skilled persons with an eye to their own objective / are not declared by speakers on statecraft to be truly divided for the king's purpose.
Where internal rebellion and external rebellion may occur for kings, / internal rebellion there is great, destructive to rulers of the earth.
Rebellion of vassals is declared by the wise to be external rebellion, O twice-born; / while from the queen, from the crown prince, and from the army commander,
from ministers, from a minister's son, and likewise from a prince, / internal rebellion is declared, terrible for rulers of the earth.
Even when a very great external rebellion has arisen, a king / whose internal circle is pure, O fortunate one, will quickly conquer his enemies.
Even a king equal to Śakra perishes through internal rebellion; / therefore, through effort, one should carefully examine one's own internal rebellion.

2.69
Puṣkara said:
Of all expedients, gift is considered the best; / by well-given gift alone, one becomes a conqueror of both worlds.
There is no one, O Rāma, who does not come under control through gift. / A generous person never falls into the domain of misfortunes, O Rāma.
Only a generous person is able to divide united enemies. / Even if men are non-greedy, profound, and ocean-like,
even though they do not accept, they become partisans. / A gift made elsewhere likewise wins others over [even when they belong] to the enemy.
Men grant that gift is the best among the expedients. / Gift is the best promoter [of success]; gift brings the highest welfare.

The generous person is always loved like a son in the worlds. / Not only do those devoted to gift conquer this earthly world alone, O hero among men; / they conquer the world of the lord of gods, O Rāma, which is very hard to conquer, the abode of the deities.
2.70
Puṣkara said:
Those who cannot be controlled by the triad of expedients / one should subjugate with punishment, for punishment is the supreme subjugator.
Its proper administration must always be carried out by a king / who is wise, possessed of good allies, and acting in accordance with the treatises on dharma.
Its proper administration would torment even the thirty [gods], / forest hermits, O knower of dharma, and destitute ascetics who are free from possessions.
In one's own country and in another's country, those learned in the treatises on dharma, / having duly investigated, should inflict punishment; everything rests upon punishment.
Whether belonging to an order of life or a caste, whether worthy of worship or a great guru, / one who does not abide by his own dharma is not immune from punishment by the king, O Rāma. / A king who punishes those who should not be punished, and fails to punish those who should be punished, / falling from his kingdom in this world, goes to hell.

देवदैत्योरगनराः सिद्धभूतपतत्रिणः ॥
उत्क्रामेयुः स्वमर्यादां यदि दण्डो न पालयेत् ॥ 2.70.10 ॥
एष ब्रह्माभिशापेषु सर्वप्रहरणेषु च ॥
सर्वविक्रमकोपेषु व्यवसाये च तिष्ठति ॥ 11 ॥
पूज्यन्ते दण्डिनो देवा न पूज्यन्ते त्वदण्डिनः ॥
न ब्राह्मणं न धातारं न पूषार्यमणावपि ॥ 12 ॥

रुद्रमग्निं च शक्रं च सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ तथा ॥ 13 ॥
विष्णुं देवगणाम्̐श्चान्ये दण्डिनः पूजयन्ति हि ॥
दण्डः शास्ति प्रजाः सर्वा दण्ड एवाभिरक्षति ॥ 14 ॥
2.14.m:
Therefore, the infliction of punishment should be carried out by a disciplined king / in accordance with the treatises on dharma, out of a desire for the welfare of the world.
Where the dark, red-eyed punishment roams fearless, / the subjects are not confused there, if the leader sees clearly.
Children, the aged, the sick, ascetics, the twice-born, the disabled, and women / would be devoured according to the law of the fishes, if punishment did not protect them.
Gods, Daityas, serpents, men, Siddhas, spirits, and birds / would transgress their proper bounds, if punishment did not protect them.
It abides in the curses of brahmins and in all weapons, / in all acts of valor, anger, and resolve.
Gods who wield punishment are worshiped, but those without punishment are not worshiped: / neither the brāhmaṇa, nor the Creator, nor Pūṣan and Aryaman;
Some men sacrifice to those who are completely peaceful in all actions, / [yet] to Rudra, Agni, Śakra, and the sun and the moon,
to Viṣṇu and the other hosts of gods who wield punishment they pay worship. / Punishment governs all subjects; punishment alone protects them.

Punishment is awake among the sleeping; the wise know punishment to be dharma. / Only out of fear of the king's punishment do the wicked refrain from wickedness;
others out of fear of Yama's punishment, and also out of fear of one another. / Thus, in the world of ordinary reality, everything rests upon punishment.
